English Morning
English Grammar
Pick out the word followed by appropriate
preposition and fill in the blank space.
The Plague ______ in London that summer and
hundreds die.
(A) Break down
(B) Broke out
(C) Break off
(D) None of these
Change the voice of the following sentence:
Are they blaming us for nothing?
(A) Are we being blamed
(B) Are we blamed
(C) Do we blamed
(D) None of these
Give the meaning of Idiom: Spick and Span
(A) meanwhile
(B) neat and clean
(C) in the meantime
(D) None of these
Choose the correct article/s from the give
options.
______ elderly couple strolled hand in hand
along ______ beach.
(A) An/the
(B) An/a
(C) Ala
(D) None of these
Choose the correct synonym Wheedle:
(A) Retreat
(B) Deceive
(C) Scar
(D) None of these
Choose the antonym of Wearisome:
(A) Refreshing
(B) Wholesome
(C) Greusome
(D) None of these
Choose the pair of words that best express a
relationship similar to that expressed in the
original question.
Man: Men
(A) Happy-Calm
(B) Duck-Ducklings
(C) Goose-Geese
(D) None of these
The sentence given below has a blank. Below
the sentence are given four options, one of
which can fill the blank complete and
meaningful. Spot it.
Either you or I ______ responsible for that.
(A) had been
(B) are
(C) have been
(D) None of these (am)
Choose the word/words that best complete the
meaning of sentence.
Through past ______ experiences, we must
prepare ______ for future challenges.
(A) interesting/ rigorously
(B) Unusual/openly
(C) bitter/ ourselves
(D) None of these
10. Choose the correct form of VERB to complete
the given sentence.
Unless you ______ hard, you cannot succeed.
(A) work
(B) will work
(C) will worked
(D) None of these
11. Complete the sentence It was the blue
car ______
(A) caused the accident
(B) cause the accident
(C) which caused the accident
(D) None of these
12. Choose the option with a correct conjunction to
complete the following sentence.
Saad is a conceited boy ______ I dislike very
much.
(A) who
(B) whose
(C) that
(D) None of these
13. Change the voice of the following sentence:
Should you look down upon the poor?
(A) Your poor must be looked down upon.
(B) Should the poor be looked down upon by
you?
(C) Should the poor looked down upon by
you?
(D) None of these
14. Give the meaning of Idiom:
To bury the hatchet
(A) to make peace
(B) to act unfairly
(C) to keep secret
(D) None of these
15. Choose the correct phrasal verb to the
complete the following sentence.
Excuse me, could I ______ this dress, please?
(A) try on
(B) try out
(C) try over
(D) None of these
16. Choose the antonym: Aboriginal
(A) Popular
(B) Modern
(C) Native
(D) None of these
17. The sentence given below has a blank. Below
the sentence are given four options, one of
which can complete and meaningful. Spot it
______ the contrary I was proud ______ it.
(A) in, of
(B) on, of
(C) at, of
